You are Koda. Build Sprint A of the InkOS performance optimization: `` primitive + 15 `loading.tsx` files so every page click shows an instant branded skeleton instead of stale UI. Stack: Next.js 16 App Router + Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui. ## Context Next.js App Router shows a `loading.tsx` file INSTANTLY when a user navigates, while the target `page.tsx`'s Server Component runs. Currently InkOS has NO loading.tsx files on the 15 main authenticated routes, so clicking a sidebar item shows stale UI for 300–800 ms. Adding these makes clicks feel instant. The skeletons must match the target page's structural rhythm — same `PageShell` padding, same header area, same tab row area, same body shape. When the real page paints, the transition should be seamless. ## What to read first - `components/shared/PageShell.tsx` — the branded page container; every skeleton should wrap with it - `components/ui/skeleton.tsx` — the primitive `` gray-animated box - `components/shared/PageHeader.tsx` — to understand the title + description + actions shape - `components/shared/PageTabs.tsx` — for tab-host pages - A few reference pages to match their shape: `app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx` (KPI + queue + agenda), `app/(app)/inbox/page.tsx`, `components/inbox/InboxClient.tsx`, `components/projects/ProjectsListClient.tsx`, `components/payments/PaymentsPageClient.tsx` ## Deliverable 1 — `components/shared/PageSkeleton.tsx` A composable primitive with preset variants. Signature: ```tsx type SkeletonVariant = | 'dashboard' // KPI cards + queue + agenda | 'list' // table with filter row | 'grid' // card grid (projects, flash events) | 'tabs' // PageHeader + tab row + table | 'two-pane' // messages: thread list + thread panel | 'calendar' // toolbar + week grid | 'hub' // AI design hub | 'chart' // reports/analytics | 'generic' // fallback: header + stacked blocks interface PageSkeletonProps { variant: SkeletonVariant fullHeight?: boolean // passed through to PageShell for calendar/messages } export function PageSkeleton({ variant, fullHeight }: PageSkeletonProps) { /* ... */ } ``` Each variant renders with `` as the outer wrapper (unless variant is 'two-pane' or 'calendar' which pass fullHeight=true by default). Use existing `` primitives inside — match the real page's visual rhythm (same heights for header, tabs, cards, rows). Keep it lightweight — ~15–30 Skeleton elements per variant is enough. Example for `dashboard`: ```tsx case 'dashboard': return ( {/* Title */} {/* Description */}
{[1,2,3,4].map(i => )}
{/* Queue heading */}
{[1,2,3,4].map(i => )}
{/* Agenda heading */}
{[1,2,3,4,5].map(i => )}
) ``` Do similarly for the other 8 variants. Keep it concise — the goal is visual match, not pixel perfection. ## Deliverable 2 — 15 loading.tsx files Each is a 3-line one-liner. Create these files: | Route | loading.tsx path | Variant | |---|---|---| | `/dashboard` | `app/(app)/dashboard/loading.tsx` | `dashboard` | | `/inbox` | `app/(app)/inbox/loading.tsx` | `tabs` | | `/calendar` | `app/(app)/calendar/loading.tsx` | `calendar` (fullHeight=true) | | `/clients` | `app/(app)/clients/loading.tsx` | `list` | | `/artists` | `app/(app)/artists/loading.tsx` | `tabs` | | `/payments` | `app/(app)/payments/loading.tsx` | `tabs` | | `/appointments` | `app/(app)/appointments/loading.tsx` | `tabs` | | `/projects` | `app/(app)/projects/loading.tsx` | `grid` | | `/messages` | `app/(app)/messages/loading.tsx` | `two-pane` (fullHeight=true) | | `/inventory` | `app/(app)/inventory/loading.tsx` | `tabs` | | `/reports` | `app/(app)/reports/loading.tsx` | `chart` | | `/flash-events` | `app/(app)/flash-events/loading.tsx` | `grid` | | `/ai-design` | `app/(app)/ai-design/loading.tsx` | `hub` | | `/marketing` | `app/(app)/marketing/loading.tsx` | `generic` | | `/consent-forms` | `app/(app)/consent-forms/loading.tsx` | `tabs` | Each file: ```tsx import { PageSkeleton } from '@/components/shared/PageSkeleton' export default function Loading() { return } ``` ## Constraints - TypeScript strict, no `any` - No `console.log` - Match PageShell padding (don't add your own) - Use only Tailwind classes; the Skeleton component already handles the gray animation - For fullHeight variants, pass `fullHeight={true}` to PageShell ## Quality gates - `pnpm typecheck` clean - Each loading.tsx renders without error when dropped into Next.js App Router ## Report - Files created (16 total: 1 primitive + 15 loading.tsx) - Any variant shape decisions you made that deviate from the plan - Typecheck result **Be fast. Don't read more than you need to. The variants don't need to be pixel-perfect — just "obviously the same shape as the target page" so the transition feels smooth.**

Wait — the background task from earlier completed with exit code 0. But the inline run showed errors. The `_fullHeight` prefix approach is fine but let me reconsider — the `fullHeight` prop is intentionally unused in the exported function because each variant sub-function hardcodes whether they use fullHeight. The `two-pane` and `calendar` variants always pass `fullHeight` to PageShell directly. The prop is there for API completeness but some callers pass it without the sub-function needing it.

A cleaner fix is to use the prop in the switch statement routing — but actually the current design is correct: `TwoPaneSkeleton` and `CalendarSkeleton` always use `fullHeight` internally. The prop on `PageSkeleton` is provided for future extensibility but currently unused. The `_fullHeight` prefix tells TypeScript "intentionally unused".
